correctness.rationale: Conditioning on j labeled origins removes their possible incoming arcs, making the mapping restricted to the n-j complementary labels exactly uniform and preserving every cycle. Summing over ordered tuples proves mixed factorial identity. Rooted-forest counting gives P(K_m=k)=k(m)_k/m^(k+1). Its survival tail grows strictly with m, implying negative covariance of every strictly increasing cyclic-core transform with origins. A dominated Riemann-sum evaluation of E[K_n]-E[K_(n-1)] gives the negative sqrt(n) constant; exact empty-bin variances give the correlation constant. Exact independent enumeration matches through n=6.

value.rationale: The numbers of cyclic points and indegree-zero vertices are canonical structural observables of a uniform functional digraph. The finite-n identity specifies their entire bivariate law through all origin factorial moments, permits conditional inference under multiple excluded targets, and proves a uniform strict negative association with every increasing core statistic. The negative covariance is order sqrt(n) despite both marginal variances being order n, exposing a nontrivial second-order dependence beyond marginal limit laws.
